result:
I thought back to the various conversations I'd had over the course of the past week. There was the intense discussion with my colleague about climate change and how it has taken a toll on our planet. Though we are still far from completely mitigating the harms inflicted upon it, there are countless individuals and communities working tirelessly to reduce our carbon footprint and conserve our natural habitats. My colleague's passion for preserving the environment and his astonishing frugality in consumer goods made me wary. "I'm an environmental protective!" he thought. His standpoint encouraged me to adopt a similar approach towards my actions and how they can impact our planet.

I also recall a heartwarming encounter with a local farmer who struggled to make ends meet. Upon learning the basis of our persisting food crisis in the U.S., to which I was astonished; we have access to food all day long, in some sense, a right to guarantee food for our citizens is severely lacking. This story made me dream of a world where everyone, regardless of their station, has access to adequate sustenance, and where we prioritize ethical consumption and fair trade systems. I wanted to be part of that change.

Similarly, our society is plagued with pervasive social issues, including racial discrimination, marginalization, and discrimination. As an advocate for human rights myself, it was essential to bear witness to the challenges my friends and acquaintances have faced solely due to their skin shade. The more I learnt, the more important it became for me to continue raising awareness and using my privilege to amplify the voices of the oppressed.

In addition to these challenges, I experienced a sense of helplessness and frustration when I observed many young students feeling hopeless in finding a sense of purpose. While traditional degrees and vocational training are still extensively sought-after paths, I recognized the need for broader education. In my vision, a universal education system that teaches critical thinking and hands-on learning beyond our set age of "schooling" could be transformative. By encouraging lifelong learning, we may fill young minds with the vital tools necessary to face and understand the world's challenges, thus building the resilience and adaptability we so desperately need.

Lastly, I remember the jovial gathering at a doctrinaire's home where funnels were turned into an ideal place to share a meal. I observed and listened as each person, from different walks of life, discussed different topics while being open to learning and understanding others. As we concluded our meal, the crackling fire faded, we decided to book dinner the following week to return for more discussions. I believes that when we value diversity in thought and ideas, true understanding and genuine connections blossom.

Reflecting on all these encounters, my soul humed with a renewed vigor to make a change in this world. A change that starts with myself, where I lead by example in the choices I make and the actions I take. The earth could use a helping hand, and hopefully, this dented me with the fuel to make it happen. I know without a doubt, collective action resonates and inspires untold impact. Inspiration for centuries has crumbled under the enormity of ignorance and indifference. Today, we rise, praying hard for the power that human compassion possesses, the power that is the colorful yet unified symbol of our shared humanity.

I understand the thought of self-improvement only serves as a foundation to this grander collective movement. Once I have honed myself, the time to cast ripples shall come. As engineers of our destiny, may we discover the balance and wisdom of the future.
